title: Claimable Lost Units on FBN Warehouse-Loss Cases: Method Statement
content:
**Method.** For Fulfilled by Northloop (FBN), the claimable lost units of a warehouse-loss case are the units on the lost-in-warehouse inventory adjustments of the case's SKU dated inside the warehouse-loss lookback and outside the warehouse-loss search hold, less the units of that SKU on found-inventory records dated inside the warehouse-loss lookback, less the units on lost-in-warehouse reimbursements of that SKU dated inside the warehouse-loss lookback; a negative remainder counts as zero, and that remainder is then capped at the warehouse-loss claim ceiling and at the claim unit cap, whichever is lower.

The case is the seller's open reimbursement case whose loss kind is lost in warehouse, and its SKU is the SKU recorded on that case. Units already reimbursed on the same source object are never claimed again.

## Quantities and values

| Quantity | Value |
|---|---|
| Warehouse-loss lookback | the lookback base of 2 months |
| Warehouse-loss search hold | 1 month, during which a lost-in-warehouse adjustment is still being searched for and is not yet claimable |
| Warehouse-loss claim ceiling | 4% (0.04) of the units of the SKU on inbound receipts dated inside the warehouse-loss lookback, rounded down to a whole unit |
| Claim unit cap | 15 units |

**Dating rule.** For the claimable lost units, a record is dated inside a span of a given number of months when fewer than that number of whole months have passed from its date to the handling date, a whole month passing on the same day number of a later month, so a span of zero months holds no record.

## Order of working

1. Lost units counted: units on lost-in-warehouse adjustments of the SKU inside the lookback, less those of them inside the search hold.
2. Remainder: the lost units counted, less found units of the SKU inside the lookback, less units on lost-in-warehouse reimbursements of the SKU inside the lookback; below zero it is zero.
3. Claimable lost units: the lowest of the remainder, the claim ceiling and the claim unit cap.

## Worked example (hypothetical records, handling date 20 May)

| Record of the SKU | Date | Units | Whole months to 20 May | Treatment |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lost-in-warehouse adjustment | 15 March | 3 | 2 | outside the 2-month lookback |
| Lost-in-warehouse adjustment | 2 April | 6 | 1 | inside the lookback, outside the 1-month hold: counted |
| Lost-in-warehouse adjustment | 10 May | 4 | 0 | inside the hold: not yet claimable |
| Found-inventory record | 25 April | 1 | 0 | deducted |
| Inbound receipts | within the lookback | 300 | | ceiling base |

Lost units counted are 6. The remainder is 6 less 1 less 0, which is 5. The ceiling is 4% of 300, which is 12. The claim unit cap is 15. The lowest of 5, 12 and 15 is **5 claimable lost units**.

With the same records but 20 counted lost units and nothing found or reimbursed, the remainder of 20 is held to the ceiling of 12, giving 12. Where found units and earlier lost-in-warehouse reimbursements inside the lookback exceed the counted lost units, the remainder is zero and so are the claimable lost units.
